sources_considered.why: Versioned primary research compares completed software tasks across model generations through early 2025.
Dated release documents additional practical functionality and its limitations.
Independent field experiment supplies material evidence against assuming capability gains always improve productivity.
Read as a research guide; the versioned paper avoids reliance on subsequently updated charts.

evidence_items.locator: Section 4.2, Model horizon length vs. release date
evidence_items.explanation: Comparative measurements extend into early 2025 and show increased ability to complete longer software tasks. The qualitative analysis also identifies better adaptation to errors and stronger tool use; these are substantive task-completion gains under the stated reading.

The release added screen-based interaction through cursor movement, clicking and typing, extending Claude's practical functionality. Anthropic explicitly described the capability as experimental and error-prone, so this disclosure is corroborating evidence rather than proof of reliable general automation.

Experienced developers were slower with early-2025 AI tools in this randomized study. It limits claims about practical benefits, but compares AI assistance with no assistance rather than testing whether successive models improved.

unresolved_gaps: The evidence does not establish improvement in every domain or broad productivity gains.
